title: Bug request contract bug-request/1, revision 2, and the factory's internal shapes
description: The machine-readable definition of every shape in docs/product/bug-request-v1.md. Every object forbids unknown fields and requires every field; a nullable field holds null. Every pattern starts with ^ and ends with $.

SafeInteger.description: An integer whose absolute value is at most 2^53 - 1.

MicroUsd.description: Money in integer micro-US-dollars (contract section 3), never negative. 1500000 is $1.50.

SignedMicroUsd.description: Money in integer micro-US-dollars that is negative only on an overrun (contract section 8.5).

Uuid.description: Lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal, chosen by the client.

GitCommitId.description: A full 40-character lowercase Git commit ID.

RelativePath.description: A relative POSIX path: segments joined by '/', with no leading or trailing '/', no empty, '.' or '..' segment, and no backslash or control character. Any other character is allowed, so source paths such as 'src/app/(main)/[id]/page.tsx' and dotfiles such as '.gitignore' are valid.

AbsolutePath.description: An absolute POSIX path inside a copy: '/' and then segments joined by '/', with no trailing '/', no empty, '.' or '..' segment, and no backslash or control character.

UtcTime.description: UTC ISO 8601 time with milliseconds and Z (contract section 3). The format adds the calendar check (no 2026-02-30, no second 60).

ItemKey.description: Chosen by the client and unique within a request (uniqueness is not checked by the schema).

Identifier.description: A non-empty identifier declared by the service, a host or a source, such as a baseline, source, entry, criterion, suite, check set, protocol or copy ID.

Description.description: A normalized request description: plain-language text with no leading or trailing white space, as String.prototype.trim leaves it, and never empty (contract section 6).

Version.description: A non-empty version label, such as "1".

CopyRunOutcome.description: How a runner's copy ended: ran (the command ran), setup_failed (the copy could not be set up, for example a file whose sha256 does not match) or timed_out (the command passed its time limit).

hosts.description: Every HostId appears exactly once: clients build the form from this list and never hard-code hosts (contract section 4).

bug_types.description: Every BugTypeId appears exactly once: clients build the form from this list and never hard-code bug types (contract section 4).

combinations.description: Every (host, bug type) pair of HostId and BugTypeId appears exactly once (contract section 4.2).

difficulty_options.description: Every DifficultyOptionId appears exactly once: source_inferable_allowed is the available default and source_only_difficulty_required is listed as unavailable (contract section 4.4).

baseline_id.description: The pinned application revision, such as umami@ec0ff503.

Criterion.description: A versioned criterion of a bug type. Its example phrases are matched exactly (contract section 6.1), and its failure code is published per criterion version (section 6.3).

example_phrases.description: Matched exactly, as word sequences (contract section 6.1).

failure_code.description: What the verification checks report on the buggy copy when a candidate demonstrates this criterion (contract section 6.3).

Combination.description: Supported means a declared source with at least one entry exists and its verification checks are implemented (contract section 4.2).

reason.description: Why the pair is unsupported (the host's availability reason when no entry is available over the planned window); null when supported (contract section 4.2).

source.description: The declared source; set when supported.

entries.description: The number of catalog entries available over the planned window [now, now + max_wall_clock_s], by the host's availability; at least 1 for a supported pair (contract section 4.2).

criteria_ids.description: The criteria that the entries available over the planned window target (contract section 4.2).

DifficultyOption.description: Source-inferable difficulty is the default and always available; source-only difficulty is unavailable, not the default, and gives a reason (contract section 4.4).

Limits.description: Service configuration; clients read limits here and never hard-code them (contract section 4.3).

max_description_chars.description: Counted in Unicode code points after trimming (contract section 5).

RequestInput.description: The body of POST /api/factory/interpretations and the input of a start (contract section 5). Limits from Capabilities are checked by the service, not the schema.

hosts.description: One or two hosts, no repeats.

items.description: At least one item; at most limits.max_items.

budget_microusd.description: Shared by every host and item; within the limits' budget range.

RequestItemInput.description: One item of a RequestInput, as the client sends it.

description.description: Any text or null. The service trims it and maps an empty result to null (contract section 6); at most limits.max_description_chars Unicode code points after trimming.

NormalizedRequestInput.description: The normalized form of a RequestInput: each description trimmed, and null when nothing is left (contract section 6). Interpretation.input carries it.

hosts.description: One or two hosts, no repeats.

items.description: At least one item; at most limits.max_items.

budget_microusd.description: Shared by every host and item; within the limits' budget range.

interpretation_sha256.description: Canonical hash of the normalized input, the interpreter, catalog, route and source versions, the factory profile and the availability result for the planned window, not the raw time (contract section 6.1).

input.description: The normalized input actually interpreted (contract section 6).

startable.description: True only when no problem has severity blocking.

items.description: Each input item interpreted, so at least one (contract section 6).

type_totals.description: At most one total per bug type. A requested type's total is the sum of its items' quantities, so it is listed and at least 1; a type no item requests has 0 if it is listed (contract section 5).

problems.description: Request-level problems, so none has an item.

description.description: The normalized description, kept verbatim (contract section 6.1).

criteria.description: Empty when the item has no description (contract section 6.1).

unmatched_text.description: Each maximal run of words that no criterion or filler phrase covers, from its first word to its last, so an entry starts and ends with a letter or digit; empty when the item has no description. Any entry makes the item unsupported with unrecognized_description, and that problem needs an entry (contract section 6.1).

eligible_sources.description: Sources on the selected hosts, at most one per host, and at least one when the item is supported. An item has none exactly when it carries unsupported_combination or no_matching_source (contract section 6.2).

status.description: Unsupported exactly when the item has a blocking problem; an item that requires source-only difficulty or has unmatched text is unsupported.

problems.description: The item's own problems, so each names an item; request-level problems belong to Interpretation.problems.

ItemDifficulty.description: An item that requires source-only difficulty is unsupported, never downgraded (contract section 4.4).

entries.description: The number of the source's catalog entries available over the planned window that satisfy the item's criteria (contract sections 4.2 and 6).

worst_case_per_candidate_microusd.description: At most one entry per host.

worst_case_per_validation_microusd.description: At most one entry per host. A startable interpretation, the kind a request freezes, has one for each host that a supported item draws from, since a validation run reserves the worst case of its case's host from the frozen interpretation (contract section 11).

item_key.description: Null for the request-level budget_below_minimum; set for every item-level code (contract section 6.2).

input.description: As the client sends it; the canonical body holds its normalized form (contract section 7).

stop_reason.description: Set only in state finished; its code belongs to the outcome.

delivery.description: Derived from the counts: complete when nothing is missing, none when no case was delivered; a fulfilled outcome always has complete.

items.description: Each request item, so at least one.

type_totals.description: At most one total per bug type. A requested type is listed with requested at least 1; a type no item requests has requested 0 if it is listed (contract section 5).

cases.description: Qualified cases of this request only; empty exactly when delivery is none.

events.description: Up to 200 events with seq greater than the after parameter. Event 1 is request_accepted. A request_finished event, at most one, names the outcome and stop code and appears only in state finished; a stop_requested event, at most one, only in states stopping and finished; validation events only in state finished.

next_after.description: The seq of the last event returned, or the after parameter when none is; at least 1, since event 1 always exists.

RequestBudget.description: Contract section 8.5. Beyond the sign of remaining_microusd, the arithmetic between the fields is not checked by the schema.

remaining_microusd.description: budget_microusd - committed_microusd; negative only on an overrun.

Funnel.description: Distinct candidates in this request (contract section 8.2).

description.description: The normalized description of the item.

requested.description: The item's quantity, so at least 1.

case_ids.description: The delivered cases that fill the item, each listed once; empty exactly when delivered is 0.

candidate_id.description: Canonical hash of source_id, catalog_version and entry_id; unique within a request.

reason.description: Set exactly for the stages rejected, invalid, incomplete and skipped, with a reason of that stage (contract section 8.3).

item_key.description: Set at requested_criteria_passed, when the candidate is assigned to an item; null for a candidate whose cells did not match in export verification (the original-suite and check reasons and bug_not_detected), one that fits no item (wrong_failure) and one skipped before it runs (duplicate_defect, no_budget_for_candidate).

case_id.description: Set exactly in stage qualified: only a qualified candidate becomes a case (contract sections 10 and 10.5).

Event.description: One event of a request, discriminated by type (contract section 8.4). Events are append-only.

CandidateEndedEvent.description: The reason belongs to the stage the type names (contract section 8.3).

criterion_ids.description: The criteria the candidate demonstrated, which become its case's criteria_met: at least one, each once (contract sections 6.3 and 8.4).

Case.description: A qualified case (contract section 10). It never carries answer-bearing material (section 10.1).

title.description: Short plain-language name of the observed failure.

item_key.description: The request item it fills; null for the completed example.

criteria_met.description: Criteria the case demonstrated in export verification; at least one (contract section 6.3).

validation.description: The latest user-started validation run, if any. A run takes the slot that the request holds until it finishes, so a case has none before its request is finished.

CaseMatrix.description: The six cells of a qualified case: every cell matched its expectation.

CaseOriginalSuite.description: The unchanged original suite passes on all three copies.

CaseVerification.description: The verification checks pass on the clean and fixed copies and detect the failure on the buggy copy.

observed.description: error when the copy could not be prepared or run; incomplete when too few runs were valid.

matches_expectation.description: True exactly when observed equals expected.

Packages.description: Both parts of a case are ready and have a download path: a case appears only once it is qualified, after its parts are verified and stored (contract sections 10 and 10.2).

pair_sha256.description: Canonical hash of the two parts' SHA-256 values and the case ID.

format.description: rbw-bug-case/1 for the bug case, rbw-validator/1 for the validator package.

download_path.description: Offer a download only when ready is true and this is not null.

request_id.description: The live request: set for live_request, null for published_example.

ValidationRun.description: POST and GET of a case's validation runs (contract section 11).

matrix.description: Null until the run finishes, and when the harness could run no cell.

cost_microusd.description: The run's cost recorded when it completed: null before state finished, set for passed and failed, and possibly null after an error whose spend is uncertain, since reconciliation updates the request's budget, not the run. Null is not 0 (contract section 11).

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every refused call (contract section 12). Clients branch on error.code, never on the message.

details.description: BusyErrorDetails for busy, InterpretationErrorDetails for interpretation_stale and unsupported_request, otherwise null.

reason.description: active is retryable; needs_reconciliation is not.

ExampleResponse.description: GET /api/factory/example. The case carries published_example provenance.

TestEvidence.description: GET /api/factory/test/evidence?request_id= in test mode: read-only evidence of one request (contract section 15.1).

TestOperation.description: One spend ledger operation of the request.

operation_id.description: The spend ledger's operation ID: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

state.description: A settled operation is terminal with settled_microusd set.

reserved_microusd.description: The operation's original reservation in every state. It is held until the operation is settled or reconciled, so the request's reserved_microusd sums only the operations still holding theirs (contract section 15.1).

settled_microusd.description: Set only in state terminal, once settled, and in state reconciled, which always records it.

TestSlot.description: The factory slot and what holds it, if anything.

holder_request_id.description: The request whose start or validation run holds the slot.

holder_validation_id.description: Set while a validation run holds the slot.

TestProviderCall.description: One call made to the fake provider.

TestReconcileRequest.description: The body of POST /api/factory/test/reconcile; the answer is the RequestStatus after reconciliation (contract section 15.1).

CatalogEntry.description: Internal: one recipe of a finite catalog. It holds answer-bearing material and is never sent to a client or a debugging agent; only presentation text reaches a Case.

criteria.description: The criteria the entry targets. Each criterion's failure code comes from the criteria catalog, never from the entry (contract section 6.3).

incident.description: The permitted plain-language description, without fix hints.

CatalogPresentation.description: Internal: the client-safe text of a Case (contract section 10.1), scanned before use; no answer material.

kit_image.description: The pinned amd64 kit image reference.

Protocol.description: Internal: a declared repetition protocol, readable from the catalog alone.

valid_trial_rules.description: Rule IDs that the host adapter's interpret() applies.

FileSet.description: Internal: a local directory and its listed files.

files.description: The listed files, relative to root.

BugCaseInputs.description: Internal: what a host adapter gives the exporter for a bug case.

source.description: The buggy application source with the unchanged original tests, without version-control history.

ValidatorInputs.description: Internal: what a host adapter gives the exporter for a validator package.

checks.description: Verification checks, fixtures and expected vectors.

clean_reconstruction.description: Turns the exported buggy source into the clean copy.

ExpectedMatrix.description: The expected outcome of every cell, as the qualification table of contract section 1 fixes them.

UnpackedPair.description: Internal: the two archives unpacked by the harness in fresh workspaces.

clean.description: Reconstructed from the exported buggy source.

fixed.description: The reference repair applied to the exported buggy source.

CopyPlan.description: Internal: what a runner executes for one copy.

files.description: The app source tree, placed at destinations.app before start.

evaluator_files.description: Validator material, placed at destinations.evaluator, an evaluator-only location.

app.description: Where the runner places every file of files.

evaluator.description: Where the runner places every file of evaluator_files; evaluator-only.

results.description: Where the copy writes its results; the runner copies this directory back.

CopyRoots.description: Internal: the local directories the harness built from an UnpackedPair, which a runner reads a copy's files from.

app_root.description: A local directory holding the plan's files.

evaluator_root.description: A local directory holding the plan's evaluator files.

CollectedCopy.description: Internal: what a runner brings back from one copy, which the host adapter's collect parses into a CopyRecord.

exit_code.description: The command's exit code, or null when there is none.

results_dir.description: A fresh local directory with the copy's results, or null.

results_sha256.description: The sha256 of a deterministic tar of results_dir, or null.

CellObservation.description: Internal: never sent to a client.

SuiteObservation.description: Internal: a CellObservation of the original suite with its test counts.

expected.description: The number of tests the suite should execute.

CopyRecord.description: Internal: what one copy's run recorded.

evidence_sha256.description: The collected copy's results_sha256, or null when the copy brought back no results. A complete record has one.

QualificationRecord.description: Internal: the qualification route's record for one candidate. Whether the verdict follows from the cells and criteria is not checked by the schema.

reason_code.description: Null for accepted; otherwise a candidate reason of the verdict's stage.

QualificationCell.description: Internal: a CellObservation with its expectation.

matches_expectation.description: True exactly when observed equals expected.
